To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the catalytic activity of the benzimidazole- oxime Pd(III)-complex is significantly enhanced by microwave irradiation and that the turnover frequency reached 42,000 under microwave irradiation.
the benzimidazole-2-oxime Pdcatalyst is a very active and versatile system for C-C cross-couples reactions in water.
a benzimidazole-based Pd(II) complex is a highly efficient catalyst for the Suzuki-Miyaura and Heck reactions of aryl bromides in water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new, efficient and environmentally friendly palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling protocols in water.
the development of novel and efficient palladium-catalyzed C-C cross-courpling reaction using water as the solvent and microwave heating.

the development of novel, highly active and selective Pd(II) and Pd(0) catalysts, which can be used in the Suzuki-Miyaura and Heck C–C cross-coupling reaction of aryl and vinyl halides in water as a solvent and under mild reaction conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the benzimidazole- oxime Pd( II) -complex is a very promising catalyst for Suzuki and Heck C–C cross-coupling of deactivated aryl- or heteroaryl halide substrates under microwave irradiation in water.

the use of water as solvent for Suzuki and Heck C–C coupling reactions is not recommended, since the reactions are not accelerated and the yields are lower compared to the reactions in organic solvents.

the benzimidazole- oxime Pd( II) complex is an efficient catalyst for the Suzuki and Heck cross-coupling of aryl- and hetereoaryl halides with phenylboronic acid and styrenes, respectively, using water as the solvent and microwave irradiation for heating.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
water is not only an efficient solvent for microwave-assisted reactions but also an excellent solvent for Pd-catalyzed Suzuki and Heck reactions.
the use of water as a solvent and microwave heating as a source of energy is a promising strategy to improve the catalytic activity of the benzimidazole-oxide-Pd complex.
the use of microwave irradiation as the energy source is beneficial to the reaction, and that the use of water as solvent is beneficial for the catalytic activity of the catalyst.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the benzimidazole- oxime Pd( II )-complex can be used as an efficient and reusable catalyst for Suzuki and Heck cross-coupling reaction in aqueous media.
the use of water as a solvent for Pd-catalyzed C-C cross-couples of aryl and hetaryl halides is a viable option, which is not possible under thermal heating.
water can be used as a green solvent for Pd-catalyzed C-C bond formation reactions under microwave irradiation.
